title: Why New Orleans lacked record companies; Dover Records royalty rates
summary: Matassa blames a lack of business entrepreneurs, himself included, says local labels were fairer to artists, and recalls paying 10% on Dover Records versus 2-4% from outside companies.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, there was a lack of business entrepreneurs, myself including. Although I was doing good with the studio and everything, I wasn't thinking forward about how to do more and marketing-wise and all that kind of thing. And I'm afraid that that kind of atmosphere prevailed in the area, too. I don't think a lot of us were thinking as real businessmen about growing and making more money and doing more things. Certainly not to the extent that we should have or could have. Right. Yeah. And for that, we have to take a lot of blame because a lot of good things that might have happened probably never happened because of that. And a lot of bad things that did happen might not have happened. You know, I'm not saying that if a New Orleans guy got his act together and started doing successful records, that he would pay people better or not. But I think that's what took place. I sincerely believe that the local guys did a better job of, with a couple of exceptions, did a better job of being honest and fair with the artists and the writers.
Would you think the locals were better than...

I think so. I said with a couple of exceptions, it was probably better not to mention names, but you probably know them as well as I do. And that could have been better. That was one of the things that, when I did finally get into the record business, one of the things that I set myself out to do was to pay people a good rate. I mean, when I started Dover Records, everybody got starting rate 10%. And let me tell you...
Right. And there were a lot of companies still coming to New Orleans, giving people 2% and 3% and 4%, and then having bad arithmetic on top of that, you know?
So, but it was... It was something lacking on our part down here especially. And in me, I have to say that I didn't do a good job in that sense at all.
